title: Policy choices and administrative details
summary: Congress may establish a governing policy and authorize another branch to supply implementing details; the boundary between the two is contested.
notes:
Grimaud uses the need for local and seasonal forest-management judgments to explain why Congress may authorize implementing rules. The responsibility to choose the governing subject, goal, and legal consequences remains central to that explanation. Gorsuch’s Gundy dissent would place greater weight on the distinction between Congress’s policy decisions and an administrator’s details.

The post-Gundy note asks whether the category can be applied consistently. Deciding whether a worker is an employee may require factual findings, legal interpretation, and a policy choice affecting a large workforce at once. An account that calls every consequential judgment a detail risks making the limit empty; an account that permits only facts devoid of judgment would threaten much ordinary administration. These are questions posed by the editors, not additional holdings of Gundy.
